lessons: Rebuild from the merge base: the closed menu table in chupa/observe.py, plus run and review admission in chupa/status.py that _admit and _review call. Review found that design sound. Keep _admit and _review behavior unchanged on each outcome.

In snapshot, read porcelain once with --untracked-files=all, or reuse the entries plan_intake reads. Derive each stem's pending flag with the tickets/<stem>/ prefix test. Never call runner.ticket_pending per stem: it starts one git subprocess per stem, about 527 stems.

validate_ticket calls _graph(repo) (chupa/tickets.py:544), which reads every tickets/*/ticket.md, so calling it per stem makes snapshot O(N^2). Build the graph once per snapshot and pass it in, for example with an edges parameter the verbs also use.

Do not run git show main: or validate_ticket per stem for the merged or settled stems that load_tickets skips, unless that row's admission result depends on them. Admission inputs must stay equal to what the verbs compute.
In tests/unit/test_menu_admission.py, assert with faked git that one snapshot makes one porcelain git status call whatever the stem count. This guards against per-stem subprocess regressions.
